findings.title: Remove unpinned remote script execution from image build
findings.whyItBreaks: The build downloads https://example.com/install.sh and executes it directly with root privileges, with no checksum, signature, version pin, or reviewed vendored copy. Any change to that response, TLS interception, DNS compromise, or upstream account takeover injects arbitrary commands into the image build, allowing dependency tampering and source exfiltration.

findings.title: Do not swallow Load errors in exported helper
findings.whyItBreaks: Load distinguishes a missing key with ErrMissing and may return an explicit empty string for a present key. LoadOrDefault discards ErrMissing and returns "" in both cases, forcing every caller of the exported API to treat failure and a real empty value identically.

findings.title: Do not leak result sends past Run completion
findings.whyItBreaks: Run starts a goroutine for every job but does not wait for its send to finish. The exported function can therefore return while all results remain unsent. A normal producer-consumer lifecycle after `Run(...)` is to close the results channel, but any pending send then panics; even without closing, the caller cannot distinguish completed work from work still racing after Run returns.

findings.title: Restore tenant-scoped record deletion authorization
findings.whyItBreaks: Substituting a non-admin session and a record from another tenant yields `false || false == false`, but any admin and any record yields `true || ... == true`; the exported predicate therefore authorizes cross-tenant deletion. It also authorizes every same-tenant non-admin regardless of record ownership.

findings.title: Stop swallowing settings parse and validation failures
findings.whyItBreaks: The catch-all converts JSON syntax errors and the explicit `bad theme`/`bad fontSize` validation failures into valid default settings. On the one existing path, `updateFontSize` then mutates those defaults and invokes `save`, so a malformed stored value is silently overwritten instead of propagating an error and leaving persistence untouched as before.

findings.title: Restore ceiling rounding for partial pages
findings.whyItBreaks: For totalItems=101 and pageSize=10, the function returns 10 instead of 11. Consumers using the exported page count cannot access the 101st item because the final page is omitted.

facts.meaning: The page count rounds down instead of up.
A remainder/partial final page is omitted or a small result becomes zero pages.
The page count rounds down instead of up.

findings.title: Keep report artifacts tied to builtFrom
findings.whyItBreaks: The report sets builtFrom to the caller-selected branch commit, but obtains artifacts from the fixed "verified" ref. Whenever those refs resolve differently, the returned report falsely pairs commit metadata with another commit's artifacts.

findings.title: Apply `limit` before returning sorted entries
findings.whyItBreaks: The unchanged public contract promises at most `limit` entries. For positive limits, the new body skips `.slice(0, limit)` and returns every entry. `renderFeed(all)` therefore can receive more than 20 entries and returns an array longer than its intended fixed page size of 20; `recentEntries(['c','b','a'], 2)` also returns three entries instead of two. Non-numeric `limit` such as `NaN` bypasses `limit <= 0` and likewise returns every entry.

findings.title: Make entry-count match rendered manifest rows
findings.whyItBreaks: renderManifest now omits stale entries from rows, but still passes entries.length to the `# entry-count:` header. For input `[{path:'a',size:1,stale:true}]`, it emits `# entry-count: 1` followed by zero data rows, making the exported manifest self-inconsistent.

findings.title: Restore exported FormatLegacyID before merging
findings.whyItBreaks: FormatLegacyID is an exported package function, so external modules may call it for the promised LEG-prefixed legacy formatting. This PR removes both the function and its behavioral test, turning an upgrade into a compile failure for those consumers; the repository's remaining FormatID caller does not replace legacy formatting.

findings.title: Restore execute instead of always throwing
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported function declares a string return but unconditionally throws for every input, replacing the prior normalization behavior with guaranteed failure.

findings.title: Reject viewers before handle can return read-only
findings.whyItBreaks: For `{ status: "active", role: "viewer", attempts: 0 }`, `handle` previously returned `"read-only"`. It now calls `isEligible` first, which rejects viewers and returns `"rejected"`, leaving the viewer branch at line 25 unreachable and regressing every active, under-limit viewer request.

findings.title: Do not require payment to save a draft
findings.whyItBreaks: canProceed previously allowed saving any draft. The added payment gate is applied by the existing saveDraft caller to an action that does not require payment, so {state:'draft', payment:'missing'} changes from 'saved' to 'blocked' even though a draft is legitimately saveable without payment.

findings.title: Return files matching the snapshot commit
findings.whyItBreaks: publishSnapshot resolves `commit` from the caller-supplied channel but resolves `files` from the hard-coded `stable` ref. The returned Snapshot therefore claims to describe `head` while exposing files from a different commit, making the public result internally inconsistent whenever those refs differ.

findings.title: Restore the defensive DataFrame copy
findings.whyItBreaks: The base implementation copied `df` before assigning values, so callers retained their original DataFrame. The head implementation assigns matching `value` cells directly to the caller's object and then returns it. Any caller using the returned result as the transformed value while also continuing to use the input now observes lost original values and hidden aliasing between the input and result.

findings.title: Restore the CI workflow under .github/workflows
findings.whyItBreaks: GitHub Actions discovers workflows only under .github/workflows. The rename moves the entire workflow definition to docs/ci.md, so pushes and pull requests no longer execute `npm run lint` and `npm test`, while README.md line 5 still claims CI runs them on every push.

findings.title: Enforce the positive-integer contract in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The public name promises a positive integer, but `s.parse().unwrap_or(0)` accepts negative values. Through `charge`, input `-1` produces `-100`, directly contradicting the declared positive-value contract.

findings.title: Remove or borrow the vector passed to `dbg!`
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items)` takes ownership of `items` and drops the returned vector, so `items.len()` on line 3 attempts to borrow a moved value and compilation fails. This breaks every caller of the public `process` API.

findings.title: Compute changed paths against the pinned revision
findings.whyItBreaks: For pinned revision A and `latest` B, the returned `fromRevision` is A but `changedPaths` contains paths computed against B. Consumers following the interface contract at lines 7-9 replay B's path list on top of A, causing the wrong files to be replayed or validated. This is an exported public API whose result contract is inconsistent even though no in-repo caller exists yet.

findings.title: Update `email` consumers for the `contact_email` rename
findings.whyItBreaks: `ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN email TO contact_email` removes `email`, while the unchanged query `SELECT email FROM users` then fails with an undefined-column error; existing persisted users are also not migrated to a newly added replacement column.

findings.title: Remove the committed billing API key and restore environment loading
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported makeClient() now returns a hard-coded live-format credential. Anyone with repository or artifact access obtains it without authorization checks, and the prior fail-fast validation for a missing BILLING_API_KEY is gone.

findings.title: Restore admin purge of archived projects
findings.whyItBreaks: The base implementation purged an archived project when user.isAdmin was true. The refactor checks `if (user.isAdmin) return "forbidden"` first, so every administrator now receives `forbidden` before reaching the archived-project check and `db.delete(project.id)` is never executed. This rejects the legitimately authorized purge action itself, not merely an unauthorized non-admin attempt.

facts.meaning: The refactored guard incorrectly returns forbidden for administrators.
Non-administrators can reach the destructive project purge/delete path.

findings.title: Restore the missing-settings default in startup
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None when the path does not exist at app/config.py:6-7. The removed None check previously replaced that with {"workers": 1, "region": "us-east-1"}; startup now evaluates None["workers"] at line 14 and raises TypeError, making missing-configuration startup fail instead of using the documented prior default.

findings.title: Do not report failed charges as successful
findings.whyItBreaks: The prior code propagated `gw.Submit` errors to the caller. The changed public path logs the failure and returns `nil`, so every caller receiving `nil` cannot distinguish a completed charge from a failed one and may treat the payment as settled.

findings.title: Restore tenant isolation in the settings cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: settingsFor still accepts a tenantId and uses it in store.fetch, but caches and looks up values using only the setting name. For the same setting name, the first tenant's value is returned to every subsequent tenant. invalidate(name) is correspondingly global and cannot remove one tenant's entry without evicting all tenants.

findings.title: Prevent concurrent reservations from overselling stock
findings.whyItBreaks: With stock=1, two concurrent reserve calls can both read remaining=1 before either resumes. Both await save(0), both return true, and the caller has approved two reservations against one unit. If the store serializes saves, the second save can also overwrite the same value, preserving the lost update.

findings.title: Remove retry's duplicate seconds-to-milliseconds conversion
findings.whyItBreaks: backoff() now returns milliseconds (1,000..30,000), but retry() still treats it as seconds and multiplies by 1000. The first failed attempt now waits 1,000,000 ms instead of 1,000 ms, and late attempts wait 30,000,000 ms instead of 30,000 ms.

findings.title: Do not discard the close error in Save
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported `Save` API previously returned `f.Close()` after a successful flush; it now schedules `defer f.Close()` without retaining its result. `Close` can surface delayed filesystem-write failures after `Flush` succeeds, so `Save` can return nil while the caller believes persisted data is valid. No in-repo callers were found, but this changes the public error contract.

findings.title: Return every row in the computed page window
findings.whyItBreaks: page_window promises all rows belonging to the page, but range(start, end - 1) excludes the final row. For rows=['a','b','c'] and page_size=2, page_count returns 2, yet page 0 returns ['a'] and page 1 returns []; summarize renders only '1. a', silently losing 'b' and 'c'.

findings.title: Return expired cache entries and evict fresh ones
findings.whyItBreaks: The age check is inverted: a fresh entry is deleted and get returns null, while an entry older than ttlMs returns its expired value. This both caches misses and serves stale data.

findings.title: Fix splice-during-forEach job pruning
findings.whyItBreaks: Splicing shifts later jobs left while forEach advances by the original index. For `[done, fresh, done]`, the final done job remains in the returned array. The mutation also changes the caller's original array.

findings.title: Preserve the zero-length guard in averageAmount
findings.whyItBreaks: averageAmount([]) now evaluates 0 / 0 and returns NaN instead of the previously defined 0, changing this exported function's established empty-array behavior.

findings.title: Do not mutate the rows argument in busiest
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.prototype.sort mutates `rows`, so callers selecting the busiest row also have their original array silently reordered as a side effect.

findings.title: Sort scores numerically before selecting the cutoff
findings.whyItBreaks: `scores.sort()` converts numeric elements to strings and sorts lexicographically. For scores `[10, 9, 100]` and `n = 2`, it produces `[9, 10, 100]`, reverses to `[100, 10, 9]`, then selects cutoff `10`; the result is `[10, 9]`, incorrectly omitting the score-100 player. The replaced comparator `(a, b) => b - a` produced `[100, 10, 9]`, so the returned top two would be `[100, 10]`.

findings.title: Use constant-time comparison for webhook signatures
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous `hmac.compare_digest` guarded `signature_of` against timing analysis. The changed ordinary `==` leaks comparison-prefix timing, making a forged signature potentially discoverable over many requests; `handle` at app/webhook.py:14 uses this result as its sole authentication check before invoking the payload processor.

findings.title: Keep ledger and balance updates in one transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The ledger INSERT commits when its transaction context exits at line 23. If either balance UPDATE at lines 10-15 then raises, the ledger record remains while the transfer is incomplete; if the first UPDATE succeeds and the second fails, the debit is persisted without the corresponding credit. The base implementation committed or rolled back all three writes together.

findings.title: Keep billing day calculations in UTC
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation produced a UTC YYYY-MM-DD key. The new implementation uses local Date fields, so the same instant can produce a different key depending on TZ. For example, 2024-03-18T23:30:00Z previously produced 2024-03-18, but in Pacific/Auckland it now produces 2024-03-19. sameBillingDay consequently classifies timestamps near UTC midnight by host-local day, changing persisted or computed billing boundaries with deployment timezone.

findings.title: Restore tenant-scoped profile cache keys
findings.whyItBreaks: readProfile is exported with both tenant and account inputs, but the module-global memo now maps account alone to a profile. The first tenant to request an account ID caches its profile; every later tenant using that account ID receives the cached tenant's Profile and its tenant field. This bypasses tenant isolation and can leak profile data.

findings.title: Stop swallowing missing-key errors as empty strings
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, a missing key propagated an error from the public load API and loadAll. Now catch maps that failure to "", so callers and loadAll consumers cannot distinguish a failed lookup from a legitimately stored empty string.

findings.title: Preserve the existing timeoutMs config contract
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported Config previously required timeoutMs. Existing callers passing timeoutMs now fail type checking because Config instead requires timeout, breaking the public API without a compatibility path.

findings.title: Treat retries as additional attempts, not total calls
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported retryBackground contract names the field retries, but the loop uses that value as the total invocation count. Therefore `{ retries: 0 }` performs no initial attempt, and `{ retries: 3 }` performs only three total calls rather than one initial attempt plus three retries.

findings.title: Do not discard all retryBackground failures
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported helper catches every thrown error and returns void on exhaustion. Callers cannot distinguish successful completion from every attempt failing, so they may treat failed work as completed.

findings.title: Handle numeric Field values before reading length
findings.whyItBreaks: The public `value` contract now accepts `number`, but line 6 reads `value.length`. TypeScript rejects `length` on `number`, and at runtime a numeric input renders `len=undefined` instead of its length.

findings.title: Do not expose the deployment token in workflow output
findings.whyItBreaks: The workflow injects secrets.TOKEN into the environment and intentionally expands it into the step's output. GitHub's secret masking is a safety net, not a valid reason to emit a credential; any masking gap, transformation, debugging change, or downstream capture can disclose the deployment token through workflow logs.

findings.title: Restore the 64 MiB buffer for Git output
findings.whyItBreaks: The diff removes maxBuffer, so spawnSync uses Node's 1 MiB default. A normal source diff larger than 1 MiB exceeds that buffer before line 140 can return its patch, making a previously reviewable PR fail. The existing 64 MiB limit was aligned with the adapter's other subprocess helpers.

findings.title: Keep Bundle.baseSha equal to the diff merge base
findings.whyItBreaks: The actual patch and changed-file set use `mergeBase`, but the bundle now reports raw `PR_BASE_SHA` or the main tip fallback. When the base branch has advanced beyond the PR fork point, `baseSha` no longer matches the reviewed diff and can direct downstream review logic to include unrelated base-branch changes.

findings.title: Restore read-only sandbox for spawned Codex
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous invocation explicitly constrained Codex to read-only mode. After removal, its effective filesystem permissions depend on CLI defaults and user/configuration overrides. For an exported wrapper that executes a supplied prompt inside caller-controlled repoPath, this turns a guaranteed read-only operation into a potential repository or filesystem write path without an opt-in flag.

findings.title: Restore PR merge-base isolation
findings.whyItBreaks: PR_BASE_SHA is the target branch snapshot, not necessarily the branch point. After other PRs merge to the target branch, `git diff baseSha HEAD` and `changedFileSet(cwd, baseSha)` include those unrelated target-branch commits. The review bundle therefore contains files and patches outside this PR, causing false findings and potentially review comments on unmodified PR files.

findings.title: Do not interpret bundle text as replace patterns
findings.whyItBreaks: String.prototype.replace interprets replacement strings containing `$$`, `$&`, `$\``, `$'`, `$n`, and `$<name>` specially. `bundle.patch` is arbitrary patch text, so a patch containing `printf "$$"` is expanded to `printf "$"` before being sent to the reviewer; the prior replacer functions suppressed this expansion. JSON candidate/bundle text can trigger the same corruption.

findings.title: Pin fallback review to the reviewed head SHA
findings.whyItBreaks: The review text and verdict are computed from `headSha`. The JSON request pins that SHA, but the fallback omits `commit_id`, so GitHub applies the review to the PR's latest commit. If the head advances while the review runs or the first request fails late, the fallback can publish a verdict computed for an older commit as though it reviewed the newer one; its inline comments may also no longer match the reviewed patch.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of inventing defaults
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported public normalization path previously threw for missing or invalid severity, category, file, title, explanatory text, suggested fix, or line bounds. It now converts such input into a Finding with severity P1, category bug, an empty file, zero line numbers, and empty required text. This erases the malformed-input signal and returns data that violates the non-empty and positive-line invariants implied by Finding.

findings.title: Restore explicit repository for workflow_dispatch PR lookup
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty, so lines 38-39 invoke `gh pr view "$PR_NUM"` without `-R`. The job has not yet run actions/checkout, the runner workspace is not guaranteed to contain a Git remote for this repository, and GH_TOKEN does not imply a target repository for gh; only GH_REPO would. Removing REPO therefore breaks repository resolution on the manual-dispatch path.

findings.title: Stop normalizing malformed reviews into empty successes
findings.whyItBreaks: A null, non-object, missing summary, or missing required array previously threw 'malformed review output'. It now returns a well-typed RawReview with an empty summary and empty findings/checked/residual_risks. Because this is an exported public normalizer, callers can no longer distinguish failed/malformed output from a legitimate empty review and may treat it as a valid PASS-like result; the error signal is forcibly conflated with real data.

findings.title: Restore PR ref resolution for manual dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, github.event.pull_request is empty: checkout falls back to github.ref (normally the default branch), while PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA are empty. The job therefore checks out code that is not the requested PR and invokes the review command without required base/head SHAs, breaking the workflow's explicitly supported manual PR-review path that previously resolved refs with gh pr view.

findings.title: Restore the git output buffer limit
findings.whyItBreaks: runLocal retrieves the entire base-to-head patch through git(); without maxBuffer, spawnSync uses Node's 1 MiB default and terminates git when a PR diff exceeds it, breaking review for valid large diffs that previously fit the 64 MiB cap.

findings.title: Keep failed reviews as failed check runs
findings.whyItBreaks: A review error now creates a neutral Needlefish check despite the summary saying it did not pass. A consumer that gates on this check can treat an infrastructure or adapter failure like a non-failing result instead of the prior failure conclusion.

findings.title: Restore trusted tool checkout before executing PR code
findings.whyItBreaks: The PR head is checked out at the workspace root and both `pnpm install` and `tsx src/cli.ts` execute it. A same-repo PR can modify the reviewer, package scripts, lockfile, or dependencies, then run arbitrary code with `GH_TOKEN`, `pull-requests: write`, and `checks: write` on a self-hosted runner. It can manipulate its own review or establish persistent runner compromise.

facts.meaning: The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.
The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.

findings.title: Canonicalize severity before validating it
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview accepts untyped external review data and maps findings through normalizeFinding at src/shared/schema.ts:132. A severity of "p1" was previously canonicalized to "P1", but now fails the exact SEVERITIES membership check and is silently returned as "P3", materially downgrading the reported risk. Missing or malformed values also move from the previous conservative P1 fallback to the least severe P3 fallback.

findings.title: Stop leaking GitHub tokens to the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Omitting `env` from `spawnSync` makes Node use the parent's complete `process.env`. Consequently, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `GITHUB_API_TOKEN` are now exposed to the external Codex process, reversing the prior credential redaction and enabling token access or exfiltration through the reviewed subprocess.

findings.title: Restore the same-repository guard for self-hosted PR execution
findings.whyItBreaks: The workflow triggers for pull_request events and checks out the PR head SHA. The removed job condition previously prevented fork PRs; without it, attacker-controlled package installation and review code can run on the self-hosted runner, enabling runner takeover and compromise of persistent runner state.

findings.title: Preserve coverage for every changed file
findings.whyItBreaks: Large reviews select at most six mapped hotspots. Without the removed tail-coverage hotspot, changed files outside those hotspots never enter a deep review and no checked entry or residual records the omission, producing an apparently complete review with silent false negatives.

findings.title: Do not discard deep-pass residual risks
findings.whyItBreaks: Each deep pass may return blocking residual risks, but the merged candidate hardcodes an empty array and no code accumulates res.residual_risks. The critic therefore sees no deep residuals and deriveVerdict can derive PASS from incomplete evidence, turning a blocking signal into a clean result.

findings.title: Avoid deduplicating findings with different causes
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing whyItBreaks from the dedup key causes two findings with the same file, start line, category, and first 60 normalized title characters to collapse even when their explanations describe different defects; only the more severe one survives and the other is silently dropped.

findings.title: Restore focus and deep forwarding in large reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: `Bundle.focus` and `Bundle.deep` are user-facing review inputs. The small path still serializes the whole bundle at lines 52-55, but the large path no longer includes `focus` or `deep` in `mapBundle`; consequently, hotspot selection cannot receive that intent. The deep prompt also no longer forwards `focus`, so explicit user direction silently changes behavior based only on the patch-size threshold.

findings.title: Prevent rounded seconds from displaying as 60
findings.whyItBreaks: For a duration such as 119500 ms, `minutes` becomes 1 and the separately rounded remainder becomes 60, so `renderMarkdown` emits `1m 60s` instead of `2m 0s`. The prior implementation rounded total seconds first and avoided this malformed display.

findings.title: Reject zero or rename the non-positive parser contract
findings.whyItBreaks: parsePositiveInteger and its thrown message promise a positive integer, but the changed guard explicitly returns 0. Callers relying on the public name/error contract can receive a non-positive result as valid.
